questions.stem: Under CSA s. 107, who must ensure that the Canadian maritime documents required under Part 4 have been obtained, and by when?
options: The master, before the vessel embarks on a voyage from a port in Canada
The owner, within 30 days after the first voyage
The Minister, before issuing a licence
The deckhand, at the start of each watch
questions.explanation: Section 107 puts the duty on the master of a Canadian vessel and fixes the time as before the vessel embarks on a voyage from a port in Canada. The authorized representative has a separate duty under s. 106(2) to arrange the inspection and meet the conditions.

questions.stem: Who must ensure that the vessel is inspected for the purpose of obtaining its Canadian maritime documents and that every term or condition on them is met?
options: The master only
The Canadian Coast Guard
The pilot
The authorized representative
questions.explanation: Section 106(2) assigns both duties to the authorized representative. The master obtains the documents (s. 107) but is not the person who arranges the inspection.

questions.stem: A vessel's safety certificate will expire in two weeks and the Minister cannot issue a new one in time. What does CSA s. 17 allow?
options: Nothing; the vessel must stop operating
The master may extend it by signing the certificate
The Minister may extend the period of validity on an application made before the document expires, if it is not feasible to issue a new one in time
It remains valid automatically for 90 days
questions.explanation: Section 17(1) says every Canadian maritime document is valid for the period the Minister specifies and that the Minister may extend it on application made before expiry when a new one cannot feasibly be issued in time. There is no automatic grace period and the master cannot extend it.

questions.stem: A 14 GT vessel carries 12 passengers. Under the Vessel Safety Certificates Regulations Division 2, does she need a safety certificate?
options: Yes, because any passenger vessel needs one
No, because Division 2 covers vessels of 15 GT or less only when they carry more than 12 passengers
Yes, because she is over 10 GT
No, because Division 2 applies only to Safety Convention vessels
questions.explanation: Section 11(1) catches vessels of 15 GT or less that carry more than 12 passengers, and all vessels over 15 GT. Twelve passengers is not more than twelve, so she stays under the Small Vessel Regulations. Safety Convention vessels are in Division 1, not Division 2.

questions.stem: A 16 GT workboat carries a crew of three and no passengers. Which regime applies?
options: Division 2 of the Vessel Safety Certificates Regulations, because she is over 15 GT, so she must hold a safety certificate
The Small Vessel Regulations workboat rules only
Neither, because workboats are exempt from certification
Division 1 of the VSCR
questions.explanation: Over 15 GT puts her in Division 2 (s. 11(1)(b)), and the SVR workboat Part covers only workboats of 15 GT or less. A workboat is not exempted by being a workboat; the exclusions in s. 11(2) are pleasure craft, special-purpose vessels, human-powered vessels and unmanned non-propelled vessels without bulk cargo.

questions.stem: Which of these is NOT one of the subjects the Minister checks before issuing a safety certificate under VSCR s. 13(1)?
options: Life-saving appliances and equipment
Shipborne navigational equipment, pilot embarkation and nautical charts and publications
Watertight subdivision arrangements and details
The master's personal radio operator certificate
questions.explanation: Section 13(1) lists the vessel's structure and machinery, watertight subdivision, load lines, fire protection, life-saving appliances, line-throwing and radio installations, navigational equipment and charts, and lights and signals. Personal certificates are held by people and are handled under the Marine Personnel Regulations.

questions.stem: A safety certificate is valid for five years. What does s. 13(2) require during that time?
options: Nothing until it expires
A new certificate each year
An inspection by the date shown on the certificate, followed by endorsement of the certificate by the Minister
An inspection only if the vessel changes owner
questions.explanation: For a certificate valid for more than one year, the authorized representative must ensure the vessel is inspected by a date determined by the Minister and shown on the certificate, and the certificate is then endorsed to show the requirements continue to be met.

questions.stem: A safety certificate lists a Near Coastal Class 2 voyage with a condition that limits operation in specified wave heights. The master wants to run a trip in conditions beyond the limit because the passengers are keen. What is the legal position?
options: The class on the front is all that matters

The authorized representative must ensure every term and condition is met, and the Minister may impose such conditions after weighing criteria such as wave height, wind, visibility and nearness to assistance
The condition applies only to the owner and not to the master
The condition lapses after one season
questions.explanation: Section 16 lets the Minister restrict service and limit voyages after weighing the intended area's criteria, including wave height and wind. Section 106(2)(b) of the Act requires the authorized representative to ensure every term or condition is met. The class alone is not the limit.

questions.stem: A passenger vessel with a safety certificate is damaged in a grounding and no longer meets all the requirements behind her certificate. Under VSCR s. 17, what must the authorized representative do?
options: Submit to the Minister without delay a report describing the damage and the measures taken, with documents, and obtain written confirmation that the requirements continue to be met
Wait for the next scheduled inspection
Keep the damage in the log book only
Tell the Minister only if a passenger is injured
questions.explanation: Section 17(1)(b) requires the report to the Minister without delay where a modification, alteration or damage means the vessel no longer meets the requirements, and s. 17(2) requires the authorized representative to obtain the Minister's written confirmation afterwards. Separately, a grounding is also reportable to the TSB.

questions.stem: Which of these must hold a radio inspection certificate under NSR s. 240(1), assuming it is not a Safety Convention vessel?
options: A 9 m pleasure craft
A 7 m fishing boat
A 15 m workboat that is not a towboat and carries no passengers
A 12 m tug (a towboat)
questions.explanation: The triggers are a vessel of 20 m or more, a towboat, and a passenger vessel (more than 12 passengers) on a voyage in sea area A1 or more than five nautical miles from shore. A 12 m towboat is caught by the towboat trigger regardless of length.

questions.stem: Where must the Radio Aids to Marine Navigation and, if required, the radio inspection certificate be kept?
options: In the owner's office ashore
In the engine room
At the main operating position of the radio installation
In the master's cabin, locked
questions.explanation: NSR s. 212(b) puts them at the main operating position of the radio installation. Each radio operator's certificate is kept on board in a readily accessible location (s. 212(a)).

questions.stem: Which entries does the NSR direct the master or deck watch officer to make in the official log book (or any log book)?
options: Only the weather
The working language for navigational safety, and the dates of steering gear checks and the dates and details of emergency steering drills
The passenger list and the fuel receipts
The compass deviation card figures
questions.explanation: Section 137(1) requires the master or authorized representative to record the working language for navigational safety matters, and s. 136(4) requires the person in charge of the deck watch to record the dates of steering checks and tests and the dates and details of the emergency steering drills. The deviation card is a separate document under s. 132.

questions.stem: A marine safety inspector asks to see the compass records of a non-pleasure vessel. What does the master show?
options: The most recent deviation card for each compass, signed and dated by the master and a deck officer, or a signed statement that the compasses are satisfactory
A card signed by the owner alone
A copy of the manufacturer's brochure
Nothing; compasses are not inspected
questions.explanation: NSR s. 132(1) sets out these two options. The manufacturer's operating and maintenance manuals for required navigation equipment must also be kept on board (s. 102(2)), but they do not satisfy the deviation card requirement.
